entry.content:
Poultry farming is one of India’s fastest-growing agribusiness sectors. India ranks among the top global producers of eggs and chicken meat. If you’re considering starting a poultry farm in India, this complete guide covers planning, investment and risk management.

Why Start a Poultry Farming Business in India?

Poultry farming offers several advantages:

1. Strong Market Demand
Eggs and chicken are affordable protein sources and are consumed across urban and rural India.

2. Quick Production Cycles
Broiler chickens reach market weight in 35–42 days, allowing multiple cycles per year.

3. Scalability
You can start small (500–1,000 birds) and gradually expand.

4. Government Support
Various NABARD schemes and agricultural loans support poultry entrepreneurs.

5. Employment Generation
The sector creates jobs in rural and semi-urban regions.

However, profitability depends on management efficiency — not just demand.

Guide to Starting a Poultry Farm

Select a model based on your budget and goals.

1. Broiler Farming

  • Meat production
  • 5–6 week cycle
  • Faster returns
  • Higher price fluctuation risk

2. Layer Farming

  • Egg production
  • Long-term steady income
  • Requires longer commitment (72+ weeks cycle)

3. Contract Farming

  • Integrator provides chicks, feed, medicine
  • Lower risk
  • Fixed growing charges
  • Lower profit margin

4. Hatchery or Integrated Farming

  • Higher investment
  • More technical knowledge required

For beginners, broiler or contract farming is usually recommended.

Conduct Market Research

  • Identify local buyers (traders, hotels, processors)
  • Study seasonal price trends
  • Analyze feed cost in your area
  • Check distance to nearest poultry processing plant
  • Understand diseases in your region

Poultry farming is highly price-sensitive. Entering without market clarity can result in losses.

Prepare a Detailed Business Plan

A proper poultry business plan should include:

  • Farm capacity (1,000 / 5,000 / 10,000 birds)
  • Land and shed cost
  • Equipment cost
  • Feed cost (60–70% of total cost)
  • Mortality assumption (3–7%)
  • Break-even analysis
  • Risk mitigation strategy

A well-documented plan is essential if you’re applying for a bank loan.

Investment Required for Poultry Farming

Approximate cost for a 1,000-bird broiler farm:

Expense Category Estimated Cost (INR)
Low-cost Shed Construction (tin roof, bamboo frame, 800 sq ft) 1,20,000
Equipment (feeders, drinkers, brooder, basic fans, wiring) 60,000
Chicks (800 chicks @ ₹40 each) 32,000
Feed (1 cycle ~1.8 kg) 65,000
Medicines & Vaccination 8,000
Miscellaneous (litter, electricity, transport, repairs) 15,000

Total Initial Investment: ₹3 – ₹4 lakhs (approx.)

Operating Cost per Cycle: ₹1,20,000

Production Assumptions:
800 chicks → 5% mortality → 760 birds sold
Average weight = 2 kg → Total 1,520 kg

Revenue (₹115/kg): ₹1,74,800 (prices can go upto 150/kg)

Net Profit per Cycle: ~₹54,800

Estimated Annual Profit (5 cycles): ~₹2,74,000

Select the Right Location

An ideal poultry farm location should have:

  • Proper drainage (no flooding)
  • Reliable electricity
  • Clean water supply
  • Road accessibility
  • Safe distance from residential areas

In hot climates, build sheds in the east-west direction to reduce heat stress. Heat stress significantly affects bird growth and mortality.

Build Proper Infrastructure

Your poultry shed must ensure:

  • Good ventilation
  • Adequate spacing (1 sq ft per broiler bird approx.)
  • Predator protection
  • Insulation for temperature control
  • Easy cleaning and disinfection

Procure High-Quality Chicks

Always buy from certified hatcheries.

Healthy chicks should:

  • Be active and uniform in size
  • Have proper vaccination records
  • Show no deformities

Low-quality chicks increase mortality and reduce feed conversion efficiency.

Implement Strong Biosecurity

  1. Restrict visitor entry
  2. Install footbaths
  3. Maintain vaccination schedule
  4. Regular disinfection
  5. Rodent and pest control
  6. Separate clothing for workers

Prevention is cheaper than treatment.

Market weight target: 2 - 2.5 kg in 35 - 42 days.

Is Poultry Farming Profitable in India?

Yes, if managed efficiently.

A 1,000-bird broiler farm can generate a margin of ₹8–₹20 per bird in stable markets.

However, profits depend on:

  1. Feed prices
  2. Mortality rate
  3. Market demand
  4. Operational efficiency

Feed alone accounts for nearly 70% of production cost. Efficient feed management determines success.

Government Schemes and Loans

You may explore:

  • NABARD Poultry Venture Capital schemes
  • Agricultural term loans
  • Mudra loans for small farmers
  • State-level animal husbandry subsidies

Tips for Long-Term Success

Long-term success in any livestock or farming venture requires patience and planning. Start small and scale gradually so you can manage risks and learn from experience. Focus on building strong relationships with buyers to ensure consistent demand and better pricing. Maintain strict hygiene standards to keep your stock healthy and reduce losses. If feasible, diversify into both eggs and meat to create multiple income streams. Most importantly, keep accurate financial records to track costs, profits, and areas for improvement.

If you approach poultry farming like a structured business it can become a reliable and sustainable income source.

entry.title: What is a Rotavator? Uses, Benefits and Types Explained
entry.summary: A rotavator is one of the most important agricultural machines used in modern farming. Also known as a rotary tiller, a rotavator helps farmers prepare land quickly and efficiently before sowing crops. By breaking, loosening, and mixing the soil, a rotavator creates ideal conditions for…
entry.content:
A rotavator is one of the most important agricultural machines used in modern farming. Also known as a rotary tiller, a rotavator helps farmers prepare land quickly and efficiently before sowing crops. By breaking, loosening, and mixing the soil, a rotavator creates ideal conditions for healthy crop growth.

In India, the rotavator has become a must-have implement for farmers because it saves time, reduces labour costs, and improves soil quality.

What is a Rotavator?

A rotavator is a tractor-mounted agricultural implement fitted with rotating blades or tines. These blades rotate at high speed and dig into the soil, breaking hard clods and mixing crop residue, weeds, and organic matter evenly into the soil.

The rotavator is mainly used for primary and secondary tillage, making it one of the most versatile farming tools available today.

How Does a Rotavator Work?

The rotavator is attached to a tractor’s PTO (Power Take-Off). When the tractor runs, power is transferred to the rotavator shaft, causing the blades to rotate. As the blades move through the soil, they:

  • Cut and loosen hard soil
  • Mix organic matter
  • Level the field surface

This process creates a fine, smooth seedbed that is perfect for planting.

Uses of a Rotavator in Farming

A rotavator is widely used for multiple farming activities:

  • Soil Preparation- The main use of a rotavator is soil preparation. It breaks compacted soil and improves aeration, which helps roots grow better.
  • Weed Control- A rotavator buries weeds and their roots deep into the soil, reducing weed growth naturally.
  • Mixing Crop Residue- After harvesting, a rotavator helps mix crop residue into the soil, improving organic content and soil fertility.
  • Seedbed Preparation- A rotavator creates a fine and uniform seedbed, ensuring good seed-to-soil contact and better germination.
  • Paddy Field Preparation- In rice farming, a rotavator is commonly used to prepare wet fields and puddle the soil efficiently.

Benefits of Using a Rotavator

Using a rotavator gives farmers multiple practical benefits in daily field operations:

  1. Saves Time and Labour - A rotavator performs ploughing, harrowing, and soil leveling in one pass.
    This reduces manual effort and speeds up land preparation significantly.
  2. Improves Soil Health - A rotavator breaks hard soil and mixes crop residue evenly.
    This improves soil aeration, moisture retention, and overall soil structure.
  3. Reduces Fuel Cost - A rotavator needs fewer tractor rounds compared to traditional methods.
    Less tractor movement means lower diesel consumption and reduced operating cost.
  4. Increases Crop Yield - Proper seedbed preparation by a rotavator helps roots grow deeper and stronger.
    Healthy root development directly supports better plant growth and higher yields.
  5. Suitable for Different Crops - A rotavator works well for wheat, rice, maize, sugarcane, vegetables, and pulses.
    Its adjustable blades make the rotavator useful across multiple cropping seasons.

Types of Rotavator

  1. Tractor-Mounted Rotavator - This type of rotavator is used with tractors and is ideal for medium to large farms.
  2. Heavy-Duty Rotavator - A heavy-duty rotavator is designed for hard soil and commercial farming operations.
  3. Mini Rotavator - A mini rotavator is suitable for orchards, gardens, and small landholdings.

Rotavator blade Types

  • L-Type Blade- Ideal for soft to medium soils, shallow tillage, and leveling; provides smooth mixing of crop residue.
  • C-Type Blade- Designed for hard, compact soils and deep tillage; offers strong cutting power and excellent aeration.
  • J-Type Blade- Best for wet, sticky, or sandy soils; durable, self-sharpening, and versatile for weed control.
  • Straight Blade- Used mainly for surface weed removal and field leveling.

Why Rotavator is Important in Modern Agriculture

With rising labour costs and the need for faster farming operations, the rotavator has become essential in Indian agriculture. It improves efficiency and helps farmers complete field preparation on time.

Government schemes and custom hiring centres have further increased rotavator usage, making this machine accessible even to small and marginal farmers.

Conclusion

A rotavator is a powerful and versatile farm implement that simplifies soil preparation and boosts farm productivity. It improves soil structure and saves time and fuel, thus offering a long-term benefit to farmers. Whether you are a small farmer or a large landowner, investing in a rotavator can significantly improve your farm.

entry.title: Rooftop Gardening- Simple, Low Cost Guide
entry.summary: Rooftop gardening is the practice of growing plants, vegetables, or fruits on building rooftops by using containers, raised beds, or vertical systems to utilize unused urban space for food production. Up to 90% reduction in “food miles” less food transportation means lower carbon emissions and fresher…
entry.content:
Rooftop gardening is the practice of growing plants, vegetables, or fruits on building rooftops by using containers, raised beds, or vertical systems to utilize unused urban space for food production.

Up to 90% reduction in “food miles” less food transportation means lower carbon emissions and fresher produce.

Rooftop gardens can cut building energy use by up to 25% through natural insulation from plants.

Urban agriculture can increase access to fresh vegetables and fruits by up to 60% in core city areas.

Top Benefits of Urban Rooftop Garden

1. In densely populated Indian cities with limited land, rooftops are often unused. Gardening turns rooftops into productive agricultural space, helping maximize land use efficiency without sacrificing urban infrastructure.

2. Growing your own food ensures access to pesticide‑free vegetables, herbs, fruits. You control what goes into your soil and plants which directly improves food safety and nutrition.

3. Major Environmental Benefits- 

  • Improve air quality by absorbing CO₂ and releasing oxygen.
  • Reduce the urban heat island effect, cooling buildings naturally.
  • Ease stormwater runoff and support rainwater harvesting.

4. Energy Efficiency- Green roofs function as insulation, helping reduce indoor temperatures and energy costs. Additionally, terrace farms often use rainwater harvesting or drip irrigation, saving up to 70–90% water compared to conventional farming systems.

5. Even small green patches can support bees, butterflies, birds and other beneficial organisms helping urban ecosystems thrive.

6. Gardening is therapeutic, lowering stress, encouraging movement and increasing well‑being. This makes terrace farming not just productive but also a source of urban wellness.

Before starting here are some Challenges You Must Know-

1. Not all building rooftops are built to support the added weight of soil, water, plants. Structural assessments and sometimes reinforcements are needed before installation.

2. Initial investment for waterproofing, containers, soil, irrigation, and infrastructure can be high especially for large plots.

3. Access to water and ensuring efficient drainage can be complicated in urban settings, and poor design can cause water seepage or roof damage.

4. Terraces are highly exposed to sun, wind, heavy rains and heat all of which can stress plants and affect productivity.

5. Legal Hurdles- In many urban areas, you may need permission from building management or local authorities before converting your rooftop into a garden.

How Anyone Can Start a Successful Rooftop Garden?

1. Choose the Right Crops Strategically

  • Beginner-Friendly Options: Leafy greens (spinach, lettuce), herbs (tulsi, coriander, mint), and fast-growing vegetables (tomatoes, chilies, radishes).
  • Vertical & Container-Friendly Plants: Cucumbers, beans, and tomatoes thrive in trellises or hanging pots, making the most of limited space.
  • Seasonal Rotation: Plan crops according to the season to maximize yield and minimize pest issues. Consider companion planting to naturally deter pests.

2. Use High-Quality Soil & Compost

Healthy plants begin with healthy soil. Use a lightweight, nutrient-rich mix of garden soil, coco peat, compost, and perlite for optimal growth on terraces. Regularly enrich the soil with compost, vermicompost, or decomposed kitchen waste to maintain fertility. Applying organic mulch helps retain moisture, regulate temperature, and suppress weeds, creating ideal conditions for strong, productive plants.

3. Efficient Watering & Irrigation

Efficient watering is essential for a thriving terrace garden. Drip irrigation or soaker hoses deliver water directly to the roots, conserving water while keeping plants consistently hydrated. Rainwater harvesting can further reduce reliance on municipal water, making your garden more sustainable. Watering during the early morning or late evening minimizes evaporation and ensures plants remain healthy even in hot conditions. Together, these practices help maintain a productive and eco-friendly terrace farm.

4. Natural Pest & Disease Management

  • Organic Pesticides: Neem oil, garlic sprays, or chili-water sprays are effective against common pests.
  • Companion Planting: Plant marigolds, basil, or nasturtiums alongside vegetables to repel pests naturally.
  • Physical Barriers & Traps: Use yellow sticky traps, netting, or row covers to protect crops from insects.
  • Regular Monitoring: Inspect plants weekly to catch infestations early before they spread.

5. Optimize Space & Rooftop Garden Design

  • Stackable Pots & Raised Beds: Use multi-level planting to increase crop density.
  • Trellises & Hanging Baskets: Vertical structures allow climbing plants to grow without taking up floor space.
  • Modular Planters: These allow flexibility as you can rearrange plants according to sunlight needs.

6. Connect With Local Community

Join local clubs or online forums to exchange tips, seeds, and tools. Consider communal terrace spaces or neighborhood garden initiatives for knowledge-sharing.

 

Urban rooftop gardens are a practical solution to many pressing issues like food security, environmental sustainability, and unutilized urban space. It empowers individuals and communities to grow healthy food, reduce environmental impact and build vibrant, green cities.

Source- WifiTalents

entry.title: Indoor Saffron Farming
entry.summary: If you are planning saffron cultivation, always keep export quality in mind from day one. Indian saffron is primarily exported to Spain, Italy, France, UAE, USA, and Gulf countries, where buyers demand- High crocin content (deep red color), Strong safranal aroma, Very low moisture, Zero contamination…
entry.content:
If you are planning saffron cultivation, always keep export quality in mind from day one. Indian saffron is primarily exported to Spain, Italy, France, UAE, USA, and Gulf countries, where buyers demand- High crocin content (deep red color), Strong safranal aroma, Very low moisture, Zero contamination or adulteration

Variety

Saffron is not grown from true seeds. You must use corms for cultivation. Common commercial varieties include Kashmiri, Iranian, and Spanish strains. For indoor saffron farming, select medium to large corms weighing between 8 and 12 grams.

Why size matters:

  • Larger corms produce more flowers
  • Flower count directly impacts stigma yield
  • Bigger corms result in better-quality saffron

 Always choose firm corms with no soft spots, cuts, or fungal marks.

Production

1. Unit Preparation

  • Disinfect the entire room, racks, and trays
  • Use plastic trays instead of wood to reduce fungal risk
  • Ensure good air circulation
  • Keep the room completely clean before every cycle

2. Placement of Corms

  • Place corms upright in trays
  • Do not use soil
  • Maintain enough spacing to allow airflow
  • Avoid any direct watering

4. Climate Control

  • Gradually adjust temperature to break dormancy
  • Maintain stable humidity

There should be strict hygiene inside the saffron unit to minimise disease risk. Entry should be restricted, and anyone entering must wear masks and use sanitisers. In case of a fungal infection, the affected bulbs should be immediately isolated from healthy ones and treated with neem oil to prevent further spread.

One cycle generally takes six to eight weeks.

Flowering - The process begins with dormancy breaking, which you achieve by slowly lowering the room temperature to trigger internal activity within the corm. Once dormancy is broken, flower buds start developing inside the corm without any visible external growth. After this stage, purple saffron flowers emerge directly from the corm without leaf formation. The plant then reaches the full bloom stage, which is very short and usually lasts only one to two days. Flowers must be removed before wilting begins to preserve stigma quality.

Harvesting

is the most sensitive and value-determining stage of saffron farming. Harvest the flowers early in the morning on the same day they bloom. Hold each flower gently and pluck it carefully to avoid damaging the stigmas.

Separate only the red stigmas by hand and immediately remove all yellow and white portions to maintain high quality. Collect the stigmas in clean, dry containers and transfer them for drying without any delay. Never wash the stigmas with water, as moisture reduces crocin content and shelf life.

All parts of the saffron flower have market value if handled properly. The deep red stigmas are sold as premium-grade saffron. The yellow and light orange parts, known as styles can be sold separately at a lower price for use in herbal products. The dried purple petals are sometimes sold for natural dyes, herbal teas, or cosmetic formulations.

Once harvesting is completed, focus on multiplying saffron corms for the next cycle. This process takes place in soil or cocopeat and generally lasts close to four months. During this time, each corm divides to form two daughter corms, which can be stored and planted again, reducing the need for fresh planting material.

Technical Parameters You Must Maintain-

  1. Temperature: 15–20°C during flowering

  2. Relative humidity: 60–70%

  3. Use cooling systems in warm climates

  4. Ensure continuous air circulation

  5. Avoid direct watering of corms

  6. Do not apply fertilizers during flowering

  7. Sanitize trays and rooms before each cycle

  8. Remove infected corms immediately

Saffron farming gives the best results when quality is the first priority. With clean practices, proper climate control, and careful harvesting, growers can produce export-grade saffron and build a profitable, sustainable business over time.

entry.title: Indoor Saffron Farming Setup Cost
entry.summary: Indoor saffron farming is becoming popular among small growers because it allows saffron cultivation in limited space with full control over temperature and humidity. Although the initial investment is higher than open-field farming, it is mostly a one-time cost. Keep in mind that it can…
entry.content:
Indoor saffron farming is becoming popular among small growers because it allows saffron cultivation in limited space with full control over temperature and humidity. Although the initial investment is higher than open-field farming, it is mostly a one-time cost.

Initial Investment

Keep in mind that it can take several years to break even with the cost of initial setup.

A home-based indoor saffron setup can be established in a spare room or insulated space. For a small unit, the setup cost generally ranges between ₹4 lakh to ₹5 lakh.

This cost mainly covers vertical racks, hydroponic trays, LED lighting, temperature and humidity control systems, insulation or a compact cold room, irrigation and misting units, and the purchase of healthy saffron corms. Once installed, the same infrastructure can be reused for several years.

Operating Cost

Indoor saffron farming has predictable running expenses. The main recurring costs include electricity for cooling and ventilation, limited labour for harvesting and stigma separation, nutrient solutions, and routine maintenance.

For a home setup, the annual operating cost usually ranges between ₹1 lakh to ₹1.8 lakh, depending on electricity usage and system efficiency. Water consumption remains low due to the hydroponic system.

Estimated Yield

  • 1000 kg of saffron corms can produce around 1 to 2 kg of dry saffron

  • A small home setup typically produces 0.3 to 0.6 kg of dry saffron per cycle

With good management, one cycle per year is common for home-based systems.

Estimated Income

Based on conservative estimates:

  • Gross income from 0.3 to 0.6 kg saffron: ₹2.1 lakh to ₹4 lakh per year

  • Annual operating cost: ₹1.2 lakh to ₹1.8 lakh

  • Estimated annual net profit: ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh

As the initial setup cost gets recovered over multiple cycles, profitability improves significantly in the long term. Selling value-added products like saffron tea, extracts, or cosmetic-grade saffron can further increase margins.

Sales Channels

Home-grown saffron can be sold through local gourmet stores, online platforms, or directly to consumers. Many small growers also supply to herbal, wellness, and cosmetic brands that prefer traceable, chemical-free saffron. Export becomes possible once quality standards and certifications are met.

Indoor saffron farming infrastructure may qualify for financial assistance under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH). Eligible projects can receive a credit-linked back-ended subsidy of 35% in general areas and 50% in hilly or scheduled regions, routed through State Horticulture Missions after approval.

entry.title: सिरोही बकरी को क्या खिलाएँ?
entry.summary: सिरोही बकरी एक मध्यम से बड़ी नस्ल की बकरी है। यह भारत के सूखे इलाकों में पाई जाती है। अच्छी वृद्धि और दूध उत्पादन के लिए इन्हें हरी घास, सूखा चारा और प्राकृतिक चारा खाने के लिए देने चाहिए। खाने के लिए उगाए जाने वाले…
entry.content:
सिरोही बकरी एक मध्यम से बड़ी नस्ल की बकरी है। यह भारत के सूखे इलाकों में पाई जाती है। अच्छी वृद्धि और दूध उत्पादन के लिए इन्हें हरी घास, सूखा चारा और प्राकृतिक चारा खाने के लिए देने चाहिए।

खाने के लिए उगाए जाने वाले कुछ हरे चारे-

आम सूखे चारे के विकल्प

बाजरा करबी
यह पेट भरने वाला चारा होता है और अच्छी ऊर्जा देता है।

चना भूसा (Gram Straw)
यह बकरियों के लिए सुपरफूड जैसा माना जाता है। दूसरे भूसे के मुकाबले इसमें प्रोटीन बहुत ज्यादा होता है और यह बकरियों का वजन जल्दी बढ़ाने में मदद करता है।

ग्वार फलगटी
ग्वार की फसल के बाद बचा हुआ सूखा चारा बहुत पौष्टिक होता है और बकरियाँ इसे चाव से खाती हैं।

मूंग भूसा
यह बकरियों के लिए पचाने में आसान होता है और सेहत के लिए काफी अच्छा माना जाता है।

अगर हरी घास या खेत उपलब्ध हों तो अतिरिक्त रूप से चराई भी कराए

सिरोही बकरियाँ सिर्फ़ घास चरने से ज़्यादा पत्तियाँ और झाड़ियाँ खाना पसंद करती हैं। ये बबूल की पत्तियाँ खुशी से खाती हैं, जिनसे इन्हें अच्छा प्रोटीन मिलता है।

धामन, शेडा घास और जंगली घास राजस्थान और गुजरात में अच्छी उगती हैं और पाचन के लिए ज़रूरी रेशा देती हैं। इसके अलावा ये विलायती बबूल की फलियाँ और कोमल नीम की पत्तियाँ भी शौक से खाती हैं।

अच्छी सेहत और दूध के लिए इन पोषण आवश्यकताओं को पूरा करना जरूरी है-

संतुलित आहार दें, जिसमें 12–18% प्रोटीन, अच्छी ऊर्जा देने वाले कार्बोहाइड्रेट और मजबूत हड्डियों और दूध के लिए पर्याप्त कैल्शियम और फॉस्फोरस हों।

साफ़ पानी और नमक के ब्लॉक (salt lick) भी उपलब्ध कराएँ ताकि पाचन सही रहे और बकरियों की सेहत अच्छी बनी रहे।

फार्म टिप्स

चराई को घुमावदार (rotational) तरीके से कराएँ ताकि घास को उगने का समय मिल सके।

सबसे अच्छे परिणाम के लिए हरा चारा, सूखा चारा (जैसे गेहूँ का भूसा) और प्राकृतिक पत्तियाँ सभी का मिश्रण दें।

सही परिस्थितियों और चारे के साथ ये बकरियाँ अच्छी बढ़वार और दूध देती हैं।

entry.title: सिरोही बकरी पालन की पूरी जानकारी

entry.content:
सिरोही एक मजबूत, मध्यम से बड़ी बकरी की नस्ल है, जो मूल रूप से गुजरात के पालतामपुर और राजस्थान के सिरोही जिले से आती है। यह नस्ल राजस्थान, उत्तर प्रदेश और गुजरात में व्यापक रूप से पाली जाती है।

विशेषताएँ: इसकी बॉडी का रंग गहरा भूरा होता है, हल्के भूरे धब्बों के साथ। इसकी फ्लैट और लटकती हुई कान, हल्के मुड़े हुए सींग और छोटे खुरदरे बाल इसे आसानी से पहचानने लायक बनाते हैं।

पुरुष बकरी जल्दी बढ़ती है और एक साल में लगभग 80 सेमी लंबाई और 70 किग्रा वजन तक पहुँच जाती है। मादा बकरी औसतन 62 सेमी लंबी और 40 किग्रा वजन की होती है।

सिरोही साल में दो बार ब्रीड होती है और रोज़ लगभग 0.5 किग्रा दूध देती है। एक ब्रीडिंग में लगभग 65 किग्रा दूध मिलता है। लगभग 60% जन्म जुड़वाँ होते हैं, इसलिए यह नस्ल दूध और मांस दोनों के लिए भरोसेमंद है और झुंड बढ़ाने के लिए बहुत अच्छी है।

सही इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर और चारा न केवल बकरियों की वृद्धि और प्रजनन में मदद करता है, बल्कि बीमारियों से भी बचाव करता है।

जब कोई किसान बकरी पालन का व्यवसाय शुरू करता है, तो उसे कुछ बेसिक इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर की आवश्यकता होती है-

बुनियादी आवश्यकताएँ-

बकरी पालन में बंद शेड सबसे महत्वपूर्ण होता है। यह अच्छी तरह हवादार, इंसुलेटेड और सूखा होना चाहिए। जमीन हल्की रेत वाली हो ताकि नमी सोख सके और खुर की बीमारियाँ न हों।

बड़ों, बच्चों और गर्भवती बकरियों के लिए अलग-अलग हिस्से होने चाहिए, जिससे चारा, स्वास्थ्य और प्रजनन का सही प्रबंधन किया जा सके। अच्छी हवा का प्रवाह सुनिश्चित करने से ताज़ा हवा मिलती है और सांस की बीमारियों का खतरा कम होता है। छत ऐसी हो जो बकरियों को तेज गर्मी और भारी बारिश से बचाए। फर्श थोड़ी ढलान वाला होना चाहिए ताकि पानी निकल जाए और सफाई आसान हो।

मजबूत और साफ़-सुथरे फीडिंग ट्रफ खाने को व्यवस्थित और स्वच्छ रखते हैं। कांक्रीट या स्टेनलेस स्टील जैसे टिकाऊ और साफ़ करने में आसान सामग्री का उपयोग करें। ट्रफ को जमीन से ऊँचा रखें ताकि गंदगी या मल से दूषित न हो। बड़ों और बच्चों के लिए अलग-अलग खाना देने से पोषण सही रहता है।

ताज़ा पानी बकरियों की सेहत और दूध उत्पादन के लिए बहुत ज़रूरी है। भीड़-भाड़ से बचने के लिए पर्याप्त संख्या में पानी के ट्रफ लगाएँ। साफ़ और गैर-जहरीले बर्तन इस्तेमाल करें और पानी रोज़ कम से कम एक बार बदलें।

छाया क्षेत्र                                                                                                              बकरियों को आराम करने और धूप से बचने के लिए जगह चाहिए, खासकर गर्म मौसम में।
शेड के अंदर या चराई के मैदान में ढके हुए क्षेत्र उपलब्ध कराएँ।
सुनिश्चित करें कि सभी बकरियाँ बिना भीड़-भाड़ के आराम कर सकें।

देखभाल–

1. साफ़-सफाई रखें

किसी भी बकरी फार्म की सेहत की नींव है कचरे का सही प्रबंधन। अगर बकरी का मल और मूत्र जमा हो जाए तो इससे अमोनिया जैसी बदबू फैलती है, जो बकरियों को बीमार कर सकती है या उनके खुर को नुकसान पहुँचा सकती है।

इसीलिए शेड रोज़ साफ़ करें। मल को फेंकने के बजाय उसे कंपोस्ट पिट में डालें। समय के साथ यह बेहतरीन जैविक खाद में बदल जाता है, जिसे आप अपनी फसल के लिए इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं या अतिरिक्त आमदनी के लिए बेच सकते हैं।

साफ़-सुथरा फार्म मतलब खुश बकरियाँ और सभी के लिए बेहतर वातावरण।

2. जगह का सही प्रबंधन

अपने फार्म को छोटे-छोटे हिस्सों में बाँटना ज़्यादा समझदारी है। इसके लिए अंदरूनी फेंसिंग का इस्तेमाल करें।
इस तरह आप बच्चों, बड़ों और गर्भवती बकरियों को उनके आरामदायक हिस्सों में रख सकते हैं।
यह घास को भी जल्दी उगने में मदद करता है क्योंकि आप यह नियंत्रित कर सकते हैं कि बकरियाँ कहाँ चरें।
सबसे महत्वपूर्ण, अगर कोई बकरी बीमार हो जाए या नया बकरी घर लाएँ, तो उसके लिए अलग “क्वारंटीन” क्षेत्र होना चाहिए, ताकि वह बाकी झुंड से दूर रहे जब तक आप सुनिश्चित न कर लें कि वह स्वस्थ है।

3. पशु चिकित्सक देखभाल

टीकाकरण और कीड़े मारने की दवा (deworming) समय पर दें, जिससे बकरियाँ सामान्य संक्रमण और परजीवियों से बची रहें।
झुंड पर रोज़ ध्यान दें। अगर कोई बकरी थकी हुई लगे या खाना बंद कर दे, तो तुरंत चिकित्सक को दिखाएँ।
बीमारी से बचाव इलाज से सस्ता है।

सिरोही बकरी पालन 5 साल का चक्र

5 साल में जन्म लेने वाली और बेची जाने वाली बकरियों की संख्या और प्रकार (अनुमान)
